title: Speaker / Audio Driver Recovery
scope: Mechanical sorting and value triage for loudspeaker drivers.
steps: Confirm the item is a speaker or audio driver before assigning recovery value.
Separate lead wire and accessible copper voice-coil material only when removal is practical and does not destroy a higher-value intact unit.
Sort the stamped or cast frame/basket with the appropriate ferrous or nonferrous metal stream after confirming the metal.
Keep the magnet assembly separate until its type is known. Do not infer neodymium, ferrite, or recoverable rare-earth content from appearance alone.
Sort terminals and small hardware by confirmed material where worthwhile, then compare labor time with intact sale or bulk scrap value.
safety: Strong magnets can pinch fingers and attract tools unexpectedly.
Ferrite magnets can chip or shatter; use eye protection during mechanical disassembly.
Do not grind, burn, dissolve, or chemically process an unidentified magnet assembly.
value_notes: Copper is commonly present in the voice coil and lead wire, but accessible mass varies widely by driver size and construction.
Steel frames and magnet back plates usually contribute bulk ferrous value.
Magnet chemistry and rare-earth content require separate evidence; photographs alone do not prove neodymium.
